contextual.summary: Access UCL gives UK-domiciled applicants from underrepresented groups a lower offer than the standard one (if UCL selects them for an offer); it is not a guaranteed offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Lower than the standard offer; the exact grades are on each course page (for the courses recorded here, one to two grades lower, e.g. A*AA becomes A*AB for Economics and A*BB for Economics and Statistics).

criteria.detail: Live in a postcode in IMD Quintile 1 (decile 1 or 2) in the datasets UCL uses in the 2027 cycle, and attend(ed) a UK state school for the A levels (or equivalent) used for your offer. UCL has a postcode checker on its Access UCL page.
Live in a postcode in TUNDRA LSOA Quintile 1 in the datasets UCL uses in the 2027 cycle, and attend(ed) a UK state school for the A levels (or equivalent) used for your offer.

Received or been registered for UK government-funded Free School Meals at some point in the six years up to the end of Key Stage 4 (age 15-16), and attend(ed) a UK state school for your Level 3 qualifications. You must have been officially registered; UCL asks you to email it within two weeks of applying to confirm.
Estranged from both parents, with satisfactory evidence from a recognised third party.
Spent time in local authority care (care experienced), with satisfactory evidence from a recognised third party. You may also qualify if you attend(ed) a UK independent school.

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible if you attend(ed) a UK state school for A levels or equivalent and one (or more) of these applies: you live in an eligible postcode; you were registered for Free School Meals in Key Stage 4 or below; you are estranged from your parents; you have spent time in local authority care. Access UCL is not a guaranteed offer scheme and eligibility does not mean you will get an offer. Most eligibility is picked up automatically from your UCAS application. UCL says the criteria are for the 2027 UCAS cycle only and may change for the 2028 cycle.

source.evidence: Access UCL is our contextual offer scheme for UK-domiciled undergraduate applicants from groups that are underrepresented at UCL.

notes: All six courses use 2027 entry: UCL's course pages show a September 2027 start and a 13 January 2027 UCAS equal-consideration deadline (UCL says applications may stay open after it). No 2028 option is shown yet.

UCL does not use UCAS tariff points: standard offers range from A*A*A to ABB depending on the course, and it asks for at least two A levels from its preferred list (which includes Geography and Psychology). General Studies, Critical Thinking and Global Perspectives and Research are not accepted, and the EPQ is not part of its standard entrance requirements (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/undergraduate/how-apply/entry-requirements).
Economics (L100) and Economics with Study Abroad (L101) require the TMUA for 2027 entry (UCL's course page and UAT-UK's official list agree). No test is listed for the other courses recorded here.
Every course recorded here asks for an A* in A level Mathematics (Mathematics with Economics also needs Further Mathematics), so Mathematics A* is the key grade for UCL.

UCL runs an Open Day Travel Bursary for eligible Year 12 state-school students who live outside Greater London and meet widening participation criteria (applications were closed when checked; https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/widening-participation/get-involved/year-12-and-13/ucl-open-day-travel-bursary).
